Read Bioscreen C output

read_bioscreen.Rd

Reads a text or csv export from a Bioscreen C plate reader and returns a tidy (long) table with one row per well per time point.

Usage

read_bioscreen(
  path,
  decimal_mark = ",",
  encoding = NULL,
  interval_hours = 1/12,
  thin_hours = NULL,
  wells_per_plate = 100,
  keep_blank = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

Path to the Bioscreen text or csv file. Compressed files (.gz, .xz, .bz2, .zip) are read directly.

decimal_mark

Decimal mark used in the file, "," or ".".

encoding

File encoding. If NULL (default) it is detected from the byte-order mark, falling back to "UTF-16LE", which Bioscreen exports use.

interval_hours

Nominal read interval in hours (default 1/12, five minutes). Elapsed times are snapped to multiples of this with snap_hours() so that timepoints match exactly across plates and runs. Use NULL to keep the reported times.

thin_hours

Optional coarser read interval in hours, for example 1/3 to keep one read every 20 minutes. Thinning happens after times are snapped to the interval_hours grid, keeps only reads that fall on the coarser grid, and requires interval_hours to be set and thin_hours to be a whole multiple of it. NULL (default) keeps every read.

wells_per_plate

Number of wells in each Bioscreen plate (100 for the Honeycomb plates).

keep_blank

If TRUE, keep the Blank column as well "Blank" (with well_index 0 and plate_id NA). The instrument reports this column as all zeros, so it is dropped by default.

Value

A tibble with columns seconds, hours, plate_id ("Plate 1" or "Plate 2", the same format as the LogPhase600 readers), well (zero-padded well within the plate, "001" to "100"), well_index (integer position in the run, 1 to 100 or 1 to 200) and od (optical density).

Details

Bioscreen exports are UTF-16LE files with two preamble lines (Label and Info), a header line (Time, Blank, then well numbers) and one row of readings per time point. Text exports separate fields with spaces; csv exports separate them with commas and quote each value. The format is detected from the header line, so both are read by the same call. The instrument computer often uses a comma as the decimal mark, which is why decimal_mark defaults to ",".

A Bioscreen run holds either one or two 100-well plates, so files contain either 100 or 200 wells. Wells 1-100 belong to plate 1 and wells 101-200 to plate 2. Wells are named within each plate by a zero-padded string ("001" to "100"), so a well is identified by plate_id and well, as for the LogPhase600 readers. The 1-200 position in the run is kept as well_index.

The Bioscreen does not report perfectly regular time intervals (for example 00:30:06 versus 00:30:05), which makes it hard to combine runs. By default times are therefore snapped onto a regular grid with snap_hours(); see interval_hours.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "bioscreen_example.txt", package = "plateReadeR")
read_bioscreen(f)
#> # A tibble: 4,000 × 6
#>    seconds  hours plate_id well  well_index    od
#>      <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>    <chr>      <int> <dbl>
#>  1       0 0      Plate 1  001            1 0.072
#>  2     300 0.0833 Plate 1  001            1 0.072
#>  3     600 0.167  Plate 1  001            1 0.072
#>  4     900 0.25   Plate 1  001            1 0.072
#>  5    1200 0.333  Plate 1  001            1 0.072
#>  6    1500 0.417  Plate 1  001            1 0.072
#>  7    1800 0.5    Plate 1  001            1 0.072
#>  8    2100 0.583  Plate 1  001            1 0.072
#>  9    2400 0.667  Plate 1  001            1 0.072
#> 10    2700 0.75   Plate 1  001            1 0.073
#> # ℹ 3,990 more rows
